# Known Issues

Repo-wide and cross-cutting issues only. Layer-specific gotchas live in dedicated
per-layer files (load only the one for your area):
- Compiler → `.github/memory/known-issues/compiler.md`
- IDE → `.github/memory/known-issues/ide.md`
- Razor → `.github/memory/known-issues/razor.md`

## Blank lines with whitespace fail linting

**Affected area:** all `*.cs` / `*.vb`
**Description:** Blank lines containing any space or tab fail lint/format; trailing whitespace also fails.
**Workaround:** Keep blank lines completely empty; run `dotnet format whitespace --folder . --include <path>`.

## Generated code must not be hand-edited

**Affected area:** `Syntax.xml`/`BoundNodes.xml`-derived `.cs`, `eng/common`, `*.xlf`
**Description:** These are produced by generators or external sync (DARC/Arcade); manual edits are overwritten or break builds.
**Workaround:** Edit the source (XML/`.resx`), then regenerate (`dotnet run --file eng/generate-compiler-code.cs`, or `/t:UpdateXlf` for `.xlf`). Never edit `eng/common` by hand.

## BuildValidator cannot replay post-compilation assembly weaving

**Affected area:** assemblies modified after `CoreCompile`
**Description:** BuildValidator reconstructs an assembly from its embedded compilation metadata. It cannot reproduce IL changes made afterward by tools such as BenchmarkDotNet's assembly weaver.
**Workaround:** Add narrowly scoped assembly exclusions to `eng/test-rebuild.ps1`; do not disable required post-compilation processing merely to make rebuild validation pass.

## IdeCoreBenchmarks requires BenchmarkDotNet 0.15 and .NET 10

**Affected area:** `src/Tools/IdeCoreBenchmarks`
**Description:** `Microsoft.VisualStudio.DiagnosticsHub.BenchmarkDotNetDiagnosers` implements the BenchmarkDotNet 0.15 exporter contract and fails to load with BenchmarkDotNet 0.16. BenchmarkDotNet 0.15 does not recognize a .NET 11 host, so the net10 benchmark executable must not use Roslyn's normal major-version roll-forward policy. BenchmarkDotNet's autogenerated runner only has a project reference to the benchmark host; central transitive pinning would otherwise replace the inherited 0.15 dependency with Roslyn's central 0.16 version.
**Workaround:** Keep the local BenchmarkDotNet 0.15 package overrides and `LatestPatch` runtimeconfig generation in `IdeCoreBenchmarks.csproj`. Benchmark validation must also override CI's ambient `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor` for this project because environment variables take precedence over runtimeconfig settings. The project copies `BenchmarkDotNet.Directory.Packages.props` to its output as `Directory.Packages.props`; keep that local policy so generated runners use the same BenchmarkDotNet version as their host.

## TODO / PROTOTYPE comments are CI-gated

**Affected area:** whole repo, PRs targeting `main`
**Description:** CI flags `TODO` comments; PROTOTYPE comments are disallowed in PRs to `main`.
**Guidance:** Do **not** add new `TODO` or `TODO2` comments. Track follow-up work as a GitHub issue and link it in code (e.g. `// See https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/NNNN`). Existing `TODO2` markers are only a frozen baseline from when enforcement was introduced — they are not a pattern to copy. Remove all `PROTOTYPE` markers before merging to `main` (allowed only on feature branches).

## `artifacts/` DLLs can be locked by lingering build servers or MSBuild node-reuse workers

**Affected area:** `folly.sh cleanse` / `folly.ps1 cleanse`
**Description:** Two independent mechanisms can leave a process holding `artifacts/` DLLs open across `folly` invocations, and they need two different fixes:
1. VBCSCompiler, the MSBuild build server, and the Razor build server register themselves as build servers and can hold an out-of-process BuildHost alive with `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.Contracts.dll` / `...MSBuild.BuildHost.dll` loaded from `artifacts/`.
2. MSBuild node-reuse (`/nodeReuse`, default `true` when running locally, per `eng/common/tools.sh`/`.ps1`) leaves worker processes running after a build so the next one can reuse them. These are a completely separate mechanism from (1) — they never register as build servers, so nothing about build-server shutdown can see or stop them. Every `folly.sh`/`folly.ps1` build action passes `--nodeReuse false`/`-nodeReuse:$false` so folly's own builds clean up after themselves, but anything that builds/tests this repo outside `folly` (a bare `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`, an IDE background build, `dotnet run --file eng/generate-compiler-code.cs`) inherits the local default and leaves worker nodes resident.

On Windows an open handle blocks deleting the DLL outright; on Unix the file is simply unlinked out from under the process, so this is invisible there.
**Workaround:** `cleanse` runs `dotnet build-server shutdown` (resolving the repo-local `.dotnet/dotnet[.exe]` first, falling back to a global `dotnet` on `PATH`) for (1), then separately pattern-matches and kills any process whose command line references both this repo's own `.dotnet` SDK root and `MSBuild.dll` for (2) — cleanse never launches a build itself, so any such match is unconditionally stale. The two steps report what they did through different mechanisms: for (1), `build-server shutdown` always reports success whether or not anything was actually running, so its own output can't say what happened -- cleanse snapshots matching PIDs before and after the call and diffs them to report a real count. For (2), cleanse enumerates workers once and kills each directly, counting only the ones `kill`/`Stop-Process` actually reports success on (not a before/after diff -- there's nothing else running that call could be racing). Either way, nothing is printed if there was nothing to report. Don't remove any of this when touching cleanse — without the shutdown/kill steps, deletion can intermittently fail on locked files with no other symptom.

`build-server shutdown` itself is not guaranteed to actually stop a server: it talks to the RPC pipe of servers registered by *the SDK it's invoked from*, so a build server started by a different dotnet install, or one whose RPC pipe is already wedged/orphaned, doesn't respond and survives the call silently while the CLI still reports success. Because of this, cleanse doesn't stop at diffing before/after PIDs to report a count for (1) — a PID gets force-killed directly (`Force-killed N build server process(es) that ignored 'dotnet build-server shutdown'.`) only once it satisfies all four: (a) it was already alive in the *original* pre-shutdown-call snapshot — a PID that only shows up in a later snapshot could be an unrelated process that started in between and must never be touched; (b) it's still alive after the shutdown call; (c) its command line references this checkout's own bootstrapped `.dotnet` SDK root, the same scope (2)'s node-reuse workers are held to — a build server for a *different* repo's checkout or SDK matches the VBCSCompiler/Razor name pattern just as easily but must never be killed, since cleanse has no way to know whether it's mid-compile for someone else's work (this scope check is case-sensitive on Unix and case-insensitive on Windows — `folly.ps1`'s `Get-PidsMatchingRegexAndSubstring` picks the comparison via `$onWindows`, matching `folly.sh`'s plain, case-sensitive `grep -F`, since two Unix checkouts can legitimately differ only by path casing); and (d) it isn't in this script's own ancestor process chain (`folly.sh`'s `_cleanse_ancestor_pids`, `folly.ps1`'s `Get-AncestorPids`, both walking the PPID chain from the running script's own PID up to PID 1) — an automation wrapper whose own command line happens to embed both the build-server name pattern and this checkout's `.dotnet` path (e.g. by echoing or defining them inline) would otherwise match its own invoking shell/CI agent and get force-killed, taking `cleanse` down with it. Node-reuse worker candidates get the same (d) ancestor exclusion, even though they don't need (a)-(c)'s survivor logic. Without the fallback at all, a build server left running by a foreign SDK or a stuck RPC pipe survives `cleanse` indefinitely with no error and no visible symptom beyond a `.NET host` process that never goes away; without the (a)-(d) scoping, the fallback itself becomes the hazard — collateral damage to an unrelated process, or worse, to the very shell running `cleanse`. The kill itself also isn't a fire-and-forget signal: both `folly.sh`'s `_cleanse_kill_pid_tree` and `folly.ps1`'s `Stop-ProcessTree` send a graceful stop first (`SIGTERM` / `Stop-Process` without `-Force`), wait up to 5 seconds, and only escalate to a forceful kill (`SIGKILL` / `Stop-Process -Force`) if the process is still alive — a count is only incremented once the PID is confirmed gone by re-checking, since the signal being delivered (a non-error return from `kill`/`Stop-Process`) doesn't mean a process that traps or ignores the graceful signal actually died.

`folly.sh` (bash) implements the PID search by shelling out to `ps | grep`, which needs two things to stay correct: (a) its own search `grep` process must be excluded from every snapshot, since the process being killed for having "VBCSCompiler" (or similar) in its command line is indistinguishable from the very `grep -Ei -- "VBCSCompiler|..."` process searching for it, which also carries that text in its own argv; (b) every `grep`/`comm` call whose match count can legitimately be zero (the common case) must be guarded (`|| true`) against `set -euo pipefail` treating "no match" as a fatal pipeline failure. Keep both when touching `folly.sh`'s cleanse.

`folly.ps1`'s process matching (`Get-ProcessSnapshot`) uses `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` on Windows and falls back to shelling out to `ps -eo pid,ppid,command` (the same source `folly.sh` uses) everywhere else. Before that fallback existed, `folly.ps1` called `Get-CimInstance` unconditionally — since that cmdlet is Windows-only WMI and PowerShell Core on Linux/macOS has no CIM server, it threw immediately and the *entire* cleanse action failed outright. This went unnoticed for a while because `folly.ps1` had never actually been run in a non-Windows sandbox; PRs touching it could only claim "written for parity, not runnable here". The `ps`-based fallback fixes that. It initially had no self-exclusion for the invoking shell: if whatever launched `pwsh` had the search text (e.g. "VBCSCompiler") anywhere in *its own* command line — not `folly.ps1`'s own invocation, but an ancestor shell's — that ancestor would match and get force-killed too. This isn't a concern for a normal terminal/CI invocation, but showed up hard when testing cleanse from Claude Code's own sandbox, where the harness wraps every Bash tool call as a single `bash -c '<entire command text>'`, so a test script that so much as defines the pattern string inline (e.g. in a heredoc) embeds it into that wrapper's own argv and makes the wrapper itself a match — which is exactly what led to adding the `Get-AncestorPids`/`_cleanse_ancestor_pids` exclusion described above, rather than leaving this as a testing-only gotcha. When testing cleanse's build-server/node-worker killing logic in an agent sandbox, still prefer launching the fake target process from a separate script file (`exec -a ... /path/to/script.sh`) rather than inline in the same tool call that contains the search pattern text — the ancestor exclusion protects the *invoking* shell chain, not a sibling test-runner process whose own argv happens to match.

## `eng/build.ps1`-only test-runner switches are not portable to bash

**Affected area:** `eng/build.sh` vs `eng/build.ps1`, `folly.sh scry` vs `folly.ps1 scry`
**Description:** `eng/build.ps1` has two switches with no `eng/build.sh` counterpart: `-testInteractiveConsole` and `$env:FOTU_TEST_RESULTS_SUFFIX` handling. This looks like `folly.sh`/`folly.ps1` parity drift, but it isn't — both exist to solve problems that only occur in PowerShell's execution model or on the Windows-only Framework test leg:
- `-testInteractiveConsole` works around `Exec-CommandCore`'s default behavior of redirecting `RunTests`' stdout and relaying it line-by-line through `Write-Output`, which makes `RunTests` see `Console.IsOutputRedirected = true` and disables its live per-work-item progress table. `eng/build.sh` invokes `RunTests.dll` with a direct foreground `dotnet exec` and no capture/relay step, so `RunTests` already sees a real inherited console by default when run via `folly.sh scry` — there is nothing for an equivalent switch to opt out of.
- `FOTU_TEST_RESULTS_SUFFIX` gives `folly.ps1 scry`'s two legs (Core + Framework) separate `TestResults`/log directories so they don't clobber each other. `eng/build.sh` has no Framework (`.NET Framework`) leg at all (`grep` for `test_desktop`/`--framework`/`framework` in `build.sh` returns nothing) — Framework tests require Windows and cannot run on Linux/macOS. `folly.sh scry` only ever runs one leg (Core), so there is no directory collision to avoid and no purpose for the suffix mechanism.
**Guidance:** Do not "fix" this by porting either mechanism to `eng/build.sh` — both would be inert no-ops there. If `eng/build.ps1` ever changes how it uses either one, re-verify this reasoning still holds rather than assuming the two scripts have simply drifted apart.

## Environmental test failures (not code bugs)

**Affected area:** full `test.sh`/`Test.cmd` runs
**Description:** A few tests fail for environment reasons unrelated to changes:
- `RuntimeHostInfoTests.DotNetInPath_Symlinked` requires symlink-creation privilege (run elevated).
- `Workspaces.MSBuild` `NewlyCreatedProjectsFromDotNetNew.Validate*TemplateProjects` fail without mobile (ios/tvos/macos/maccatalyst) dotnet workloads installed.
**Workaround:** Prefer targeted test projects; treat these specific failures as environmental.
